utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One additional matter before I get back to the report. It's come to my attention through the Court officer that Mr. Theunens is working on the time line chart that the Chamber had requested. Because I don't have any contact with him outside of this courtroom now, I just ask:

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when you've completed that, if you could just mention it at the beginning of a session, whether it's today or Monday, whenever it is, and we'll deal with it at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Black. And then to you too, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we are going to move to another topic now. It begins on page 126 of your report, which is page 146 of the B/C/S. There you devote several pages to a discussion of JNA assistance to the RSK TO. We will look at a few documents in a moment, but could you just summarise what kinds of assistance the JNA gave to the RSK TO during the first half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the first half of 1992, and more specifically the February to April time period, the SSNO, so the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence, and also of course the JNA, which was subordinate to it, provided support in three areas. First of all, organisational aspects, which includes also standing operating procedures. Secondly, the JNA and SSNO assisted in the provision of personnel. And thirdly, SSNO and JNA provided logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps we could look at document 65 ter number 1210, which has the B/C/S ERN 02077072 to 7088. Mr. Theunens, when this is brought up, hopefully in the English view on the screen in front of you, could you then tell us what this document is and whether it relates to one of those kinds of assistance which you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. When we look at the second page --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I would just note, Your Honours, that at least what I see on my monitor is in B/C/S rather than in English. I don't know if you have the same situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mine is in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: The English is on the LiveNote screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. One thing about e-court, Your Honour; I'm still learning. You may be ahead of me, but I'm told that it's actually possible on our personal computer screens to pull up -- you actually have the choice of the B/C/S or English and decide ourselves. We don't need to try to do that now, but just in the future maybe we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have that choice right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you could continue. Sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the heading on the left top corner of the document indicated is an order issued by the Federal Secretariat for National or for People's Defence, also known under the acronym SSNO, dated the 27th of February, 1992. And as we could already identify from the cover page, this is an order which deals with organisational and what is called establishment changes in the RSK TO. I will not go, unless you request me to do, into detail for the order, but when you go through it, it lists various units and commands of the RSK TO, both at the RSK level as well as lower level. And therefore it indicates that the structure of the RSK TO in February 1992 is determined by the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The Federal Secretariat for People's Defence or National Defence, to what government does that pertain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Federal Secretariat for People's Defence is part of the government of the SFRY, Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could that be given a number and admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 62, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1300. The B/C/S ERN is 02076683 to 6684.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order of the 9th JNA Corps, also known as the Knin Corps. I correct myself, it's not an order, it's a regular combat report, which is sent to the 2nd Military District command operation centre. The 2nd Military District was created, established end of 1991, early 1992, and covered the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the exception of a small section of eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina. I would like to draw your attention to the last paragraph of this regular combat report, page 4, where we see that -- we can move to the top of the page, please. Okay. Where we see that the order is signed by Major General Ratko Mladic. And for the topic we are discussing, the underlined part is the most relevant. It shows that among the commander's decisions is the continuation to -- of assisting the Territorial Defence staff and the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and he talks about not only organisational and establishment changes, as we already saw in the SSNO document we just discussed, but also Mladic mentions equipping the Territorial Defence and Ministry of Interior units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you be able to interpret what "Glina, the town of Drnis and its environs" means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the line here, it's not 100 per cent clear. Normally, during military operations, Your Honour, once -- I'm talking about offensive operations - for example, an attack - once an objective is taken, there is always a risk that there will still be resistance pockets of the enemy somewhere, so then cleaning, or even cleansing, as it is sometimes translated into English, cleaning is used in the context of removing these resistance pockets in order that they don't threaten -- they don't represent a threat for you any more. Now, on the other hand, as I've seen from other military documents, "cleaning" can also be used in the context of cleaning; i.e., that once an area has been taken, there may be, for example, dead animals, and somebody has to remove them because otherwise you have diseases. The military is the only force in the area can be involved in that, so it can also be used in that context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But are you able -- are you able to say in the context of this document what that -- what that might mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not able to say so, Your Honours, even though I don't think that, for based on what I know from the situation in Drnis, that "cleaning" is used here in the context of cleaning up resistance pockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 63, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1324, and the B/C/S ERN is 02076818 to 6830. Mr. Theunens, when this appears on the screen, could you please tell us what the document is and whether it relates to one of the kinds of assistance that you mentioned a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order from the chief of the personnel administration at the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence, and it deals with personnel support. So in the order approximately 72 officers are being mentioned; senior officers, junior officers, and I believe also some non-commissioned officers. And these people are ordered to join the RSK TO at various levels. Some people are sent to the Main Staff, others are sent to different units. And these people are obviously all JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that be given a number and admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 64, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1314. The B/C/S ERN is 01065887. Mr. Theunens, again when this appears, could you please tell us what it is and whether it relates to one of the kinds of assistance that you mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this relates to the third aspect of or the third domain of support the SSNO and the JNA provide to the RSK TO. Namely, logistical support. As we discussed earlier today, the second phase of the Vance Plan foresaw the withdrawal of the JNA and HV from the UNPAs. Now, for what the JNA is concerned, this order dated the 3rd of April 1992 indicates that real estate and material were handed over to the RSK TO before leaving the area, and this document, this order then clarifies the procedure that needs to be applied for this handover.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that please also receive a number and be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 65, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, moving to a new topic now, beginning at page 130 of your report, which is page 150 in B/C/S, you address what you call the transformation of RSK TO units into RSK special police, or PJM brigades. First before we look at the documents, why transform units from TO into police units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the answer to that question is actually given by the Vance Plan. As we discussed, the second phase of the Vance Plan stipulated the demobilisation, disbanding and disarming of the Territorial Defence, RSK Territorial Defence, and only -- and also stated that only a lightly armed - so only equipped with sidearms - police force would be allowed. Now, by transforming TO into police, you actually circumvent this stipulation of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps we could look at the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's really -- it's not a question that the answer can be found in the Vance Plan. It's a question of a response to the Vance Plan by way of circumventing some of the requirements of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps we could look at the first document on this topic, which is 65 ter number 244B. The ERN in B/C/S is 02170670. Perhaps while that is being brought up I could again ask you, Mr. Theunens, to summarise, I guess, or to give examples of different ways in which this transformation occurred. Is that something you could do without -- before we see the document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this transformation was done by moving people from one unit to another; i.e., officers who have -- had been in command or had been part of TO units were transferred to these PGM [sic] brigades, and to the outside world then looked like policemen. Less sophisticated was the repainting of vehicles, so there are orders that indicate that military vehicles that had been used by the JNA and/or the TO were repainted in order to look like police vehicles. And this happened also to some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you look at the document on your screen now, please, and tell us what is shown in this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a proposal for promotion for Colonel Borislav Djukic. This proposal is done by -- and we see that on the second page -- the proposal is sent by the president of the RSK, Goran Hadzic. Hadzic had become president of the RSK early 1992 when he replaced Milan Babic. One of the reasons for the removal of Babic was that he refused to accept the Vance Plan. Now, when we go back to the first page of the document, and we go a bit down in the document, we see in the first sentence, Borislav Djukic is identified as an infantry colonel. You may recall from documents we reviewed yesterday that he was, during the latter half of 1991, the commander of the 221st Motorised Brigade of the JNA, which was active in the area of Knin. And in this proposal, when we scroll further down in the document, we see in the last paragraph on page 1, that Djukic was, after the proclamation of the RSK, appointed assistant minister of interior and also commander of special police units of the RSK. So this order -- this proposal for promotion provides one example of a senior officer of the JNA who is transferred to the RSK police following the adoption of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I take you to a previous point. You mentioned repainting of vehicles to circumvent the requirements of the Vance Plan. But you also mentioned that the Vance Plan required that the police use light vehicles and light ammunition and not heavy things. In this process of circumventing the Vance Plan, what would happen to a repainted vehicle, like the one that appears at page 184? Your coloured pictures, Mr. Black, what you gave yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would still not pass as a light vehicle for police use, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I should have been more precise. The repainting concerned jeeps, trucks and light APCs, so armed personnel carriers on wheels. Not heavy weapons because, of course, the UN peace forces would immediately recognise it. Heavy weapons like this one should have been placed in weapon storage areas under dual key system I explained earlier. And there are some examples of repainting in documents mentioned in my report, and as I said it concerns jeeps, trucks and APCs. Now an APC has also can be used for transport of troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is an APC?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An armed personnel carrier, Your Honour. I don't have a picture with me, but the APCs I'm talking about were, for example, of the BOV type, and I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is a BOV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have a picture with me, but I can bring it with me after the break, if you allow me to go to my office. It looks like a jeep but an armoured, bigger wheels. There are less windows. I mean, there is more armour on it. It can transport a number of soldiers, or policemen even, and it can be equipped with anti-aircraft defence weapons or machine-guns and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will return to the vehicle on page 184 near the end of his testimony and discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I need to ask for this document that's on the screen to receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 1322. The B/C/S ERN is 04006412. Mr. Theunens, please tell us what this document is and whether it relates to any of the types of transformation that you discussed earlier, that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is another order from Major General Ratko Mladic. At that time commander of the 9th Corps. And he talks about the provision of arms and equipment for police units of Republika Srpska Krajina. This order covers two aspects of support. It covers the aspect of personnel. Under the heading 1, if we scroll a bit down on the document, okay, it mentions that corps wartime units have been selected to be deployed to the police departments. And if we go further down, it mentions that these -- that if people are transferred, that complete personal equipment has to be issued, including ammunition for personal arms, and arms that people can be issued with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 67, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Next document is 65 ter number 1862. The B/C/S ERN is 02805183 to 5185.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report from the Republika Srpska Krajina Ministry of Interior, and on the last page, which is page number 5, we can see that it comes from Minister Milan Martic. It dates from the 19th of May 1992. From the document as such, it is difficult to conclude to whom it is addressed, even though Martic, in the report, makes a number of requests that are addressed to the SSNO, so the Federal Secretariat for People's Defence. Several aspects in relation to the structure of RSK special police units and their transformation are being discussed. And when you look at the heading 1 alpha, which starts on the second page, the top of the second page -- I'm not sure that that is the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can we see the prior page, just to check, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. In my copy it's on two pages but here, I apologise, it's on 1 alpha. Martic also makes a number of recommendations with regard to names of MUP, Ministry of Interior units, and their subordination. When we scroll further -- and I assume this will be on the top of the second page --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Actually, before you move on, what does it say about the command -- if we could go back to that page, I apologise. The bottom of the first page in this translation, what does it say about the command of those police units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the MUP brigades or the police brigades are to be under the command of the RSK MUP, Ministry of Interior in peacetime, and in wartime, and that's in accordance with the RSK constitution discussed earlier in my report, they are to join the RSK Serbian army and be under RSK Serbian army Supreme Command. Now in wartime, Martic recommends that a special battalion is to be formed from the Knin police brigade and this special battalion has to remain under RSK Ministry of Interior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who is the RSK minister of the interior at this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, Milan Martic is the minister of interior of the RSK. And Your Honours, on the bottom of -- or further down on this page, it will be then on the next page, on page 2, there is mentioning when we -- at the bottom of this paragraph, you see, for example -- so we have heading 2, the following has been implemented. At the bottom, it says, "Police units have so far received hundred motor vehicles that have been painted." If we go further down in the document, it also mentions that JNA commands, according to Martic, failed to pay the MUP reserve troops for the month of April, so it indicates that payment for the reserve troops of the Ministry of Interior has to be done by the JNA. And Martic also complains or highlights a number of other pledges, apparently, that have not been fulfilled, like the supply of 20.000 firearms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, why would RSK MUP reserve members be paid by the JNA, if you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not analysed the functioning of the RSK Ministry of Interior, nor financial issues related to the forces that are part of that Ministry of Interior, so I'm not in a position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you gave three areas in which the JNA or the SSNO provided assistance to the RSK, one of which involved personnel. Would the payment of the MUP -- RSK MUP not be part of that assistance to personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be, Your Honour, but I want to be very clear: In the report, I only looked at military aspects. It may well be, and I would refer therefore to other witnesses, that the support FRY, or SFRY and subsequently FRY, were providing to the RSK went much further; that they maybe also provided economical support, medical support. And these are issues I didn't look at in detail, so I can only limit myself -- or I can only talk about purely military aspects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This paragraph says, "The JNA commands failed to pay the MUP reserve troops for the month of April even though the deal was that the MUP members would hold the combat lines until the JNA units withdrew to their new locations." So the MUP here are actually not operating as police people; they are operating as part of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a correct observation, Your Honour, which is also corroborated by a report we may discuss later by the Secretary-General of the United Nations in September 1992 when he informs the Security Council about the progress in the implementation of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the observation of the Chamber is correct, what in your view -- or in your view, would it be conceivable, therefore, that the RSK MUP would have then been entitled to payment from the SFRY under the auspices of the three-legged assistance that was being given to the RSK by the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only refer to this document, this document, Your Honour, that according to Milan Martic there is an agreement about the payment of forces of the Ministry of Interior of the RSK that took over the positions of the JNA. I'm not in a position to make a general assessment on how the members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbian Krajina were paid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying you're not in a position to help this Chamber to put each piece, or as many of the pieces of evidence as come before into the general picture of the broad policy and mission of the SFRY and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my report, there is a document that was drafted by the RSK Ministry of Defence Spanovic in November 1992, and maybe we will come to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We can look at it right now. Do you know the 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, before we leave the documents on the screen, could I have that admitted into evidence and be given a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let the document be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number. Are you going to want it removed now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Even though we are still talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Theunens wants to refer to another document. If it pleases, Your Honour, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I defer to your superior knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I defer to yours, Your Honour. If this could be given a number now, I think that would make things easier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when you find it, if you could please tell us the 65 ter number or the ERN range of the document you'd like to look at.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 248, and it's mentioned in my report on page 157 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. At the bottom of page 157. We have the document now on the e-court monitor. These documents -- is a note drafted by Mr. Spanovic, who was the minister of defence of the RSK at the time. Notes of talks that the RSK political leadership had with Slobodan Milosevic, the president of Serbia, on the 12th of November 1992, and when we go a bit further into the document, I think it's the third paragraph - we have it now on the bottom of the monitor - according to these notes drafted by Spanovic -- I will read from the screen: "President Milosevic said that funds for maintaining equipment should be planned via the army of Yugoslavia, and he also said that he would help in the implementation of this, and that the army of Yugoslavia should finance the active officers and civilians who stayed behind in the Krajina." Now, the reason why I was reluctant to answer your question initially, Your Honour, is that I didn't analyse how this payment or how this pledge to pay, to provide payments, was implemented. I can mention in the Milosevic case there was a financial expert who had also been trained to analyse financial issues, who provided an expert report on that issue. My, if I could call it like that, mandate in this, for this report, did not include analysis of financial support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you recap on the three areas of assistance that you said was being given by the SFRY. Just mention them, don't discuss them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. Your Honours, based on the documents I reviewed we can broadly divide them into three categories. The first category is the provision of guidelines and even orders for organisational -- on organisational issues, and also standing operating procedures. The second aspect covers the provision of personnel. And the third aspect covers logistical support, which includes the provision of ammunition, weapons, vehicles, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. Then I think my question must fall by the wayside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please give an exhibit number to this document that's been called on the screen and admit it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 69, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: A further document on this topic which we can look at quickly, 65 ter number 1864. The B/C/S ERN is 02807718 to 7719. Mr. Theunens, please tell us what this document is and whether it relates to one of the kinds of transformation that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order by the RSK municipal TO staff in Benkovac - Benkovac is located in the vicinity of Knin - dated the 11th of September 1992. And under the heading "Hereby I order" a number of instructions are given by the commander, and I would like to draw your attention to the heading number 5, which should be on the second page. This talks about what we discussed earlier, so logistical support whereby JNA vehicles that have remained behind, because by that date, 11th of September 1992, the withdrawal of the JNA has been completed, so that JNA vehicles are being handed over actually to the TO. So it's not really a transformation of TO into police, it is more support by the JNA and the SSNO to the TO in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could that receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 70, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'll begin at page 132, which is 152 of the B/C/S. Mr. Theunens, you give some more details about two particular examples of personnel. Just if you could quickly name the two people that you discuss there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I discuss Colonel Milan Novakovic and Colonel Borislav Djukic. For Colonel Borislav Djukic, we saw a document that indicated that he was transformed from an infantry colonel who had been a brigade commander, that he was transformed into a commander of a special police brigade. In the report I provide additional documents that illustrate this transformation or reassignment, and the same applies to Colonel Milan Novakovic, who, for example, in July 1992, was a commander of a tactical group of the RSK -- of the RSK that participated in operations in Bosnia-Herzegovina to assist in establishing the so-called Posavina corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'll just ask you to look quickly at two documents that relate to Djukic. The first one is 65 ter number 2070. The B/C/S ERN is 04142892 to 2893.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a -- this document is a certificate issued by the Ministry of Interior of the Republika Srpska Krajina. It is signed, as we can see on the last page, by Milan Martic, and it is a certificate to Borislav Djukic, who by then is a major general in the infantry, JNA infantry, to show or to prove that Djukic has been assigned to the post of Major General, or to the rank, actually, of Major General in the Knin PGM administration. "PGM" stands for "special police milicija," which was the name commonly used among other units but in particular for the TO units that had been transformed into police units in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you tell us which page of the document it is? I didn't see that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, it's on the first page of the document, that the information I provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 132 of the report? Or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I meant of the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So on the first page you see the duties of Djukic and his rank at the time of the drafting of this document, 30th of September 1992. And it also mentions, and I didn't pay attention to that, at the bottom of the first page, that Djukic would like to be assigned to the 1st Military District which was part of, at that time, the VJ, so the armed force of Serbia Montenegro, with headquarters in Novi Sad. I believe that it was called 1st Army at that time, but that's not a key issue. It shows that JNA officers who were transferred to the PGM still had an opportunity to return to the VJ, so the successive structure of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, one further question, just to clarify: If we go to the top of this first page, from -- all the way to the top, please, it says that -- well, who is the originator of this document, which administration?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police units, PGM administration of the Ministry of Interior of the Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who signs this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Martic. That's visible on the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask you if this is really a signature on the original Serb document. It's just a stamp and the name Martic. It may not be signed. Could we look at the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: In Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's correct, Your Honour. The translation says "signed and stamped," but I think when you look carefully on the B/C/S version, because this is a scanned document, I think there is an indication of a signature but it's largely covered by the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have difficulty seeing a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be helpful, we could try to pull the actual original document from the evidence unit, if you want to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We could do that at the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we have the original. In some cases all we have is a photocopy, but we can get the best original copy. What we have in the evidence unit, we can bring that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what would be the significance of whether or not this document is signed and stamped or only stamped? What does that signify?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally -- Your Honours, normally you would need both. A signature without a stamp can also raise issues of authenticity in the sense that in these official organisations, the stamp is used to confirm that it comes from that administration, and then the signature, of course, identifies the person who signed the document. Now, without a signature, it is difficult. It could even be just a draft document then if it's not signed, although it's unusual to stamp a draft document. Now, it can also happen, and I'm talking now about military documents, that the name has already been put under the document but that somebody else signs, and then, of course, it should be indicated that the other person -- for example, if the commander isn't there, then the chief of staff of a unit from brigade level onwards is authorised to sign, and he should say then for the commander. I've seen also that sometimes the "for" is forgotten, so -- but again it best would be to have both indications, the stamp and the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless you have further questions, maybe we can come back to this when we have the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a procedural question: Would you prefer to mark this for identification now and then we can admit it or not admit it at the time, or should I just leave it and we can come back and number it later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's mark it for identification. Then we will come back to it. May it be given an MFI number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be MFI number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could look now at 65 ter number 1867, with the B/C/S ERN 02808671, 8673. Mr. Theunens, when you've found that document, could you just briefly tell us what this document is and what it signifies. There it's come up on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]

And it concerns the solemn oath of police cadets, an order to organise this ceremony. When we go to the last page, which should be page 5 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could see the preceding page, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, Your Honours, when we go a bit downwards we can see who signed the document. It is again Borislav Djukic who signs here as commander of special units command in Knin, and he also has the title of deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could that be given a number and admitted into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document may be given -- I beg your pardon, the document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 72, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I won't ask to look at the other documents that refer to Djukic and Novakovic. They are referred to in the report. Move to another aspect of this, could we look at 65 ter number 1852, please. The B/C/S ERN is 02032603 to 2619. And Mr. Theunens, when it comes up on the screen, could you please tell us what it is and whether or not it relates to this issue of transformation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is, as it is mentioned, a newsletter, so it's used for morale and informative purposes, of the 70th Infantry Brigade of the, at that time still the RSK TO. And it mentions in the document, if we scroll into the document, next page, it should -- I think it's on the second or the third page. So it gives a history of the Plaski TO Brigade but the part we are interested in covers the spring 1992 time period, so I think if we could further scroll down. Okay, further scroll down. I think we have to go to the next page. We still have to go down. I apologise. It takes more time but I don't have the hard copy with me so it takes a bit -- still next page - takes more time. Okay. We scroll down. Yes. Mm-hmm. Okay. Now we go to the next page. We go to the bottom of the page. We go a little bit upwards. Okay. Thank you. It mentions there that it illustrates a process we mentioned earlier, transformation of TO units into PGM units, where in this paragraph it states that the brigade, so the Plaski TO Brigade, was - and it may have received another name in the meanwhile - but was demobilised between 24th of August and the 15th of -- 24th of July and the 15th of August 1992, and as the text says, at the same time, re-established as a PGM battalion, special police milicija, and the brigade was established according to peacetime establishment, as it is said in the document. So this just illustrates the transformation of TO into PGM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it PGM or PJM?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, PJM. I'm sorry, Your Honours, it should be a J.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's all right, because we are now getting G on the screen instead of J.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. It's the French influence. So wherever I said "PGM" it should be "PJM."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope the interpreters hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that clarification. Could this document receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and please give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 73, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: One further document on this same issue is 65 ter number 2072, B/C/S ERN 04143152 to 3154.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this is an order for demobilisation, which is issued by, as we can see at the bottom of the document, Lieutenant General Milan Torbica - I think it's on the third page - who was at that time the commander of the RSK TO. When we go back to the first page of the document, so we see to whom the order is addressed, the 6th zone of STO and logistical base, and just below that we see what Your Honour already mentioned. If you could stop, could go up a bit again. Okay. What Your Honour already mentioned earlier, that there is indeed a handover of TO to PJM for what is called the front line duties. And this handover is also explained under the heading 1, where it's clearly stated the front line is being taken over by the PJM forces. Further on in the order, Torbica gives additional instructions on how this order has to be implemented. He mentions, for example, under the heading 5, that people working at the TO headquarters and commands and another institutions have to wear civilian clothes. Now, that clearly illustrates that there is an effort to demilitarise, but it doesn't -- it shows actually the contrary of a disorganisation or of a disbanding as was prescribed by the Vance Plan because the structure still remains active, even though the units would probably be demobilised or they have been transformed into PJM. Commanding officers who have not been reassigned to the PJM, they remain in the TO commands and other institutions, albeit in civilian clothes, working according to timings indicated in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document also receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May we please give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 74, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before we leave section 3 of the report, there is one more document, Mr. Theunens, which you actually referred to earlier. It's 65 ter number 1360, and the ERN is 00242533 to 2544.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Actually I know, Your Honour, that we don't have a B/C/S translation of this UN report. It was admitted into Milosevic and we just recently realised that there is no B/C/S version. The relevant passages, however, are contained in the report and therefore they were translated into B/C/S when the report was translated into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. Are we getting this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you please tell us what this is and what relevance it has.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report I mentioned earlier. It's a report by the Secretary-General of the United Nations to the Security Council, to inform the members of the Security Council of the status of implementation of the UN Resolutions 743 and 762. More specifically, the Secretary-General informs the Security Council about the status of implementation of the Vance Plan. When I was working in the UNPROFOR UNPF headquarters, so from December 1994 until October 1995, similar reports were also drafted, and there I learned that the information that is included in the report is based or is provided by the people on the field. So members of UNPROFOR, the force commander and his staff, and members of UN civil affairs and political affairs, they will send a draft report to the department of peacekeeping operations within the UN, and then there may be an exchange of questions and answers to further improve the report, and this report is then used as the basis for the report the Secretary-General sends to the Security Council. This report is -- this particular report is important because the Secretary-General of the United Nations informs the Security Council of the problems, serious problems, that are created by the PJM units. And this is more specifically visible in the paragraphs 4, which is on the next page, where the Secretary-General provides information on the status of the demilitarisation phase of the Vance Plan, and he in the middle, in the body of the paragraph, he talks about the special police, or what we have identified earlier as the PJM, and he basically provides the same information as we have been going through by looking at JNA, VJ and SAO Krajina TO and MUP documents. The Secretary-General even uses the word "paramilitary forces" in his report. And he uses that in an illegal context. More information is also provided in the paragraph 6, which is on the next page. And in paragraph 6, the Secretary-General specifically addresses the protection of the non-Serb population who are still living in the UNPAs. The Secretary-General uses the expression "ethnic cleansing by paramilitary units." I would also address -- like to address -- ask, or draw your attention to the paragraphs 10 to 18, where according to the heading in the report, the Secretary-General, acts of terrorism are being discussed, and these acts of terrorism go much wider, of course, than the process of transformation of TO into PJM, but they directly refer to the situation as it is within the UNPAs. In the context of my report, paragraph 14 is quite relevant, because it directly addresses the situation in Sector South. Sector South, which covers the part of the entity known as RSK going from the area of Knin towards the north, and it mentions, for example, incidents related to the deterioration of law and order and that the non-Serb population is specifically targeted by these incidents. Paragraph 17 shows the relationship between the regular civil police in the -- or the regular RSK civil police in the UNPAs and the special police, or PJM. Now, unless you want to address the other paragraphs in the report, I would like to move to paragraphs 34 and 35. In paragraph 34, Your Honours, the UN Secretary-General writes that the main cause of the deterioration of the situation in the UNPAs has been the Knin -- what he calls the Knin authority's decision to create new paramilitary forces. These paramilitary forces are the PJM we discussed earlier and which are mentioned in the beginning of the report. Paragraph 35 is also quite important because it addresses the third phase of the Vance Plan, maintaining peace and security in order to allow a return of refugees. And particularly the end of the paragraph is quite revealing in the context of what I mentioned when we looked at the map and I spoke about various military operations Croatia had launched against a number of pink zones. I don't think the Secretary-General wants to create any justification for Croatia. On the contrary, I mean this report dates from long before the military operations, but the UN Secretary-General wants to draw the attention of the members of the Security Council on the serious implications the way the Knin authorities are implementing the Vance Plan may have in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is given -- is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 75, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I think we are at the time for the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are at the time for the next break, and if it is convenient for you, then the Court will adjourn and it will reconvene at half past 12. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we can once again attend to housekeeping matters, the Chamber has received information that the interpreters are willing to sit for an extra session this afternoon but they suggest that we go up to 1.30 for this session and take a one-hour lunch break, to 2.30, and then start from 2.30 to 1545 this afternoon. I guess that would be okay with everybody. So it seems like a sound suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That seems acceptable to the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's acceptable to the Defence as well, and we hope that the expert witness will also be able to follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. Then sometime during this week, our case had been removed from the schedule on Monday the -- on the 6th and 7th of February. Just in case the parties might have received a schedule where we were removed, I just want to remind you that we are back on schedule on those days. And not only that, we have also been given two extra days, on the 9th and 10th of February. Are we in a position to proceed on those two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are. But I would inquire, are those certain or are those tentative, the 9th and the 10th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They have written that it's in here to be confirmed. They will be confirmed if we can say we can take them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Certainly; then that's no problem. We can fill those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can fill those days?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We agree, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will then sit on the 6, 7th, 9th, 10th of February. Okay, thank you. That's all the Bench -- the Chamber had in terms of housekeeping. Over to you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: As we said we would do, we went to the evidence unit to try to find the best copy of what's been marked as MFI 1. Unfortunately, we don't have the original. We just have our -- our original is actually a photocopy. We don't have the actual with ink on it, but perhaps -- I don't know if Your Honours would like me to hand up the best copy that we have to Your Honours to look at the signature, or perhaps pass it to the witness to see if he can discern a signature there. However you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if you can pass a copy -- I see you seem to have two copies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: No, it's two pages of one document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if it can go around, I would imagine that the Defence would also like to have sight of it. If you can first give it to the witness and then to the Defence, and then you can hand it up to the Court. Let's just have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With the usher's assistance, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. The suggestion is also that it could be put on the ELMO, then we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Ah, very well. Just a reminder, Your Honours, you'll need to press "video evidence" now to see the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We may still be having technical problems. I'm not sure. Perhaps the usher can, by looking at the monitor, adjust and move the ELMO machine itself. That should -- there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, by looking at that copy of the document that's on the ELMO now, can you discern whether or not it has a signature?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, maybe I can show it with my pen, but there is a signature with -- which, based on the poor quality still, taking into account the poor quality of the copy, corresponds with what I've seen as the signature of Milan Martic on other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see what looks like a signature on that. I've seen that kind of sign on documents that are purported to be signed by Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And if I understand well, now we have the document where there are doubts about the signature, but I think, again taking into account the poor quality of the scanned copy, that when you start at the top, there is something that looks quite similar to what could be identified as a signature on the first document that was put on the ELMO, and maybe we can put them both together with the signature block.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, to be clear, I believe these are two pages of one document. I'd ask the witness just to read the ERN numbers that appear at the top of both of those pages, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the ERNs are 0414-2893 and 0414-2892.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, those correspond to the ERN range of 65 ter number 2070. On this basis I would now ask that it be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is then admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 71, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are finished with those documents. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we are now ready to move to the final section of your report, section 4, which deals with the Serb army of Krajina, or SVK. This starts at page 139 of your report, which is page 158 in the B/C/S. Consequently I want to shift your focus now away from the Territorial Defence to the SVK. First of all, tell us what the SVK was and when it was established, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, SVK stands for Srpska Vojska Krajina. It means Serbian armed forces of the Krajina, and it was actually an armed force conceived as the successor structure of the RSK TO which, in the meanwhile, had been transformed largely into PJM units. The creation of the SVK consisted of two phases. First of all, we have a number of changes to the constitution of the RSK which are adopted on the 18th of May 1992, and then we have a number of orders that are issued in October-November 1992, which implement these changes to the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we don't need to look at each of those documents. I just note that they are discussed at pages 141 to 143 of the report in English; 160 to 164 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did the Accused Milan Martic hold a rank in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, on page 143 in the English version of the report, at the bottom, I make reference to 65 ter number 713, which is a decree for an extraordinary promotion of Milan Martic to the rank of Colonel General of the Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. This decree is signed by Goran Hadzic who was at that time the president of the entity known as the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If I could ask you to pause. A document has just come up on our screen. If it could be put in the English version, please. Is this the document that you're discussing, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And when we scroll a bit to the bottom, we can see who signed -- we see the contents of the decree and also who signed it. Your Honours, this document is dated the 16th of July 1992. Even though the decree doesn't include any reference to the reasons for this extraordinary promotion, when we look at events that were taking place in the area during that time period, we can link this promotion of Milan Martic to his involvement in the operations in the so-called Posavina corridor in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 76, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next exhibit I'd like to look at, or the next document, pardon me, is 65 ter number 712; B/C/S ERN 02170842 to 0843. Mr. Theunens, could you please tell us what this document is and whether it relates to what you're now discussing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a letter from Ministry of Interior of the RSK, office of the minister, signed by the minister himself, Milan Martic, as we can see on the last page, which is page number 4. When we go back to the first page, we see that the letter is addressed to a number of political authorities in the Banija and Kordun area. Banija and Kordun are located in the area of Croatia north of the Bihac enclave; i.e., more or less covered by Sector North in the map we discussed earlier. And when we go to the first paragraph of the document, we see that Milan Martic makes reference to the fact that he and his associates are, and I quote, "On a distant and very difficult front in the areas of Derventa, Modrica and Poljaci waging decisive battles for the future, honour, religion and dignity of the Serbian people in both Serbian Krajinas." The areas of Derventa, Modrica and Poljaci are located in an area we also know as the Posavina corridor. Posavina refers to valley of the Sava River, the Sava being the border there between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia. And when Milan Martic speaks about both Serbian Krajinas, it means the Serbian Krajina on the territory of Croatia as well as the Serbian Krajina in the western part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, also known as Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, thank you. We'll return to the topic of the Posavina corridor in a few minutes. But just so -- could you tell us, does this rank that Martic held, does that mean he had a position in the SVK with troops under his command, or what's the significance of that rank, if any, that you can discern?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the documents I reviewed, it is only after Milan Martic became president of the RSK in January 1994 that he occupied a function of de jure authority over the armed forces. I have not been able to locate any documents indicating that between the date of promotion to Colonel General and January 1994 Milan Martic exercised command over military units except for the times when he and what is called in this document his associates were involved in operations in the corridor, the Posavina corridor. These operations in the Posavina corridor took place during two time periods; June-July 1992 and November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have more details on the Posavina corridor in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I neglected to ask that the last document we showed on the screen be given a number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 77, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, sticking now with the de jure elements of command over the SVK, who was the ultimate commander of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the president of the RSK was the Supreme Commander over the SVK. And this was further specified in April 1993, when the RSK Assembly adopted a number of amendments to the constitution, and one of these amendments created the RSK Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, we could look at 65 ter number 1391, which is a decision dated 22nd April 1993. The B/C/S ERN is 02166103. If we could please see the English on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go down a bit in the document, we see what the document is about. This is -- as I mentioned, this is the decision to promulgate a number of amendments to the constitution of the RSK. Amendment number XIV - so Roman 14 - determined the composition of the RSK Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If we could please see the next page in the English version on the monitors. Thank you. Mr. Theunens, can you walk us through? I think it may be even the next page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the next page. I would prefer to address these amendments in the order that I addressed them in my report, which is not the same as the one in the document. So amendment 40 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, we paused because we heard the signal for an emergency message, which I can't hear. I think the Court officer is trying to figure out what's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. I was wondering what was happening. We are still trying to determine what it is but it looks like an emergency warning about water somewhere

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Shall I proceed, Your Honour, or should we wait?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe let's wait because then we are going to cross with these people. It's now been determined that it is actually on water. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise for the interruption. I believe you were proceeding -- you were going to direct us to amendment 14 and tell us what's said there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, amendment 14 to the RSK constitution determines the members of the RSK Supreme Defence Council. The RSK Supreme Defence Council will have five members -- shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't even understand it. Maybe we should proceed and rely on the Court officer to warn us if we need to take action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Black, I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just saying that because I couldn't understand the message, maybe we could proceed and the Court officer would warn us if we needed to take action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Just to warn you, it is a water -- about -- there is a warning about water. The warning says please don't drink the water. I guess the ones in your jugs you might drink now because -- but I suppose the water they mean is don't go and drink water from the taps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to continue, so amendment 14 lists the members of the RSK Supreme Defence Council, so five members; the president of the republic, the Prime Minister, the minister of interior, the minister of defence, and the commander of what is called the Serbian army of Krajina. When we go back to the beginning of this document, amendment 13 -- actually, it's just one page back, or the top of this page, so amendment 13. Amendment 13 clarifies the responsibility of the president of the republic now that this Supreme Defence Council has been established, and it states that the president of the republic leads the armed forces in peace and wartime in accordance with the RSK constitution and with decisions of the RSK Supreme Defence Council he presides. So it means that the RSK -- the president of the republic presides the RSK Supreme Defence Council and, of course, he's the Supreme Commander. Amendment 12 states that the commander of the Serbian army of Krajina will be appointed by the Assembly of the RSK on the proposal of the RSK Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document receive a number and be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Another document on the same topic is 65 ter number 2077, the B/C/S ERN I believe is 03639756 to 9800. Mr. Theunens, this is a somewhat longer document, so if you could again help us to identify which passages are relevant to us.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, so these are amendments -- no, I apologise. The amendments that were done or that were adopted to the RSK constitution were then also reflected in the RSK law on defence which was adopted on the 20th of April 1993. I make reference to the most relevant Articles at, least from the context of my report. In my report, the Articles 8, 40 -- for example, 40, if we scroll down a bit, states that the president runs the army in peace and wartime in accordance with decisions of the Supreme Defence Council. The reference to the RSK constitution is not included but I don't think that is an issue. Article 41, which is not included in this translation, maybe it comes further, but any way you see also Article 42, for example, these are all straightforward articles of a law on defence that further detail the amendments to the RSK constitution that had been adopted before. And we can conclude from both the RSK -- both the amendments and the law on defence that the president of the RSK leads the armed forces in peacetime and in wartime in accordance with the RSK constitution and the decisions of the RSK Supreme Defence Council, which he presides.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 79, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, beginning at page 155 of your report, which are pages 175, 176 in B/C/S, you note that following his election as the RSK president, Mr. Martic replaced the commander of the SVK. Who did Milan Martic name as the new SVK commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Martic named a Major General Milan Celeketic as the new commander of the SVK, and he did this, based on the document I saw, in accordance with the suggestion of the RSK Supreme Defence Council. I would like to add that Milan Celeketic was a JNA officer who was born in the part of Serbia known as Vojvodina. So he comes from Kikinda. I mention this because quite often, in the documents we discussed earlier, when we spoke about personnel support, the people that were sent, or some of them even volunteered, to serve in the RSK TO or the SVK were people who had been born in Croatia or in the area known as the Krajina. This does not apply to Milan Celeketic as he was born in Kikinda, a village in Vojvodina, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps we could look at 65 ter number 1872. ERN in B/C/S is 02804585. Mr. Theunens, could you look at this document and tell us if it has relevance to what you just said.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this is the confirmation of what I just explained, and the decree mentions the date of appointment, that's the 22nd of February 1994, and it was Milan Martic who signed the decree as president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this receive a number and be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 80, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 261. ERN in B/C/S is 02011845. Mr. Theunens, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a decree on a special or an extraordinary promotion of Milan Celeketic. On the same day as he was appointed commander of the SVK, he's also promoted to a higher rank, the rank of Major General in the Serbian army of Krajina, and the decree is signed by the president of the republic, Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could this be given a number and admitted, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 81, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Another document, 65 ter number 1873, has the ERN in B/C/S of 02077368, if we could please see that one. Mr. Theunens, what does this document tell us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is a written record of the handover of powers from Mile Novakovic, who was the previous commander of the SVK, to Milan Celeketic, who is the new commander of the SVK. It also shows, when we look at the last paragraph, that Milan Martic was involved in this handover process, as doing a transfer of duty. As the document states, all corps commands were toured or visited, and then during the final transfer, Novakovic to Celeketic, Milan Martic was present as well as other -- as well as, excuse me, senior SVK officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 82, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Final document on this particular subissue is 65 ter number 1874. The B/C/S ERN is 02806584. Mr. Theunens, when it appears on the screen if you could please tell us what this document shows us and include the date of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report from the Main Staff -- or the General Staff, excuse me, of the Serbian army of Krajina, in which a member of the Main Staff informs the members of the SVK that Major General Milan Celeketic has been promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General by decree of the president of the republic, Milan Martic. This promotion to Lieutenant General happens, when we think back of the documents we discussed earlier, a bit more than one year after the promotion of Milan Celeketic to Major General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number and be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 83, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, from page 156 up until page 168 of your report - those pages are 177 to 187 in the B/C/S translation - you discuss the relations between the SVK and the VJ. Now, my first question for you, before we spoke of the JNA and now we speak of the VJ. Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in April 1992, when FRY was declared -- FRY consists of Serbia and Montenegro; FRY stands for Federal Republic of Yugoslavia -- then also the armed forces were transformed from VJ -- excuse me, from JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, into VJ, Vojska Jugoslavija, armed forces of Yugoslavia. There were also a number of doctrinal changes but I don't think we need to address them here. So it's just the successor structure of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Just briefly, could you summarise the relationship between the SVK and the VJ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I reviewed, Your Honours, these relations were in fact a continuation of the relations that already existed between the RSK TO and the JNA. I mean by this that the VJ continued to provide support to the SVK. This support consisted of personnel support, logistical support - so officers were sent, logistical supplies were provided - as well as what I call operational support. What I mean by this in the report that it's not the use or the deployment of combat units but the fact that members of the Main Staff of the SVK and members of the General Staff of the VJ meet to discuss operational issues. These things are discussed in the report under the heading Coordination Mechanisms. From the documents I reviewed, it's clear that there were meetings between the staffs to coordinate certain issues. There was also -- it is also clear that operational reports from the SVK, we called in military language, daily sit-reps, situation reports, were sent from the SVK to not only the General Staff of the VJ but also certain political leaders in FRY, including the president of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic. And when I say "VJ," more specifically, the chief of General Staff of the VJ, General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What role, if any, did the Accused Milan Martic have in these SVK-VJ relationships?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
